title: The servants testify
summary: Lamoni has his servants testify to what they saw. After hearing of Ammon’s faithfulness in preserving his flocks and his power against those who sought to slay him, Lamoni is astonished and asks whether Ammon is the Great Spirit. The servants say they do not know whether he is the Great Spirit or a man.

explicit_facts.text: Lamoni caused his servants to stand forth and testify to what they had seen.
Lamoni learned of Ammon’s faithfulness in preserving his flocks and his power in contending against those who sought to slay him.
Lamoni was astonished and asked whether Ammon was the Great Spirit.
The servants said they did not know whether Ammon was the Great Spirit or a man.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The servants stand before Lamoni while testifying.
unspecified_visual_details: The servants’ number and appearance
The setting’s appearance

spoken_dialogue.text: Surely, this is more than a man. Behold, is not this the Great Spirit who doth send such great punishments upon this people, because of their murders?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Lamoni

spoken_dialogue.text: Whether he be the Great Spirit or a man, we know not; but this much we do know, that he cannot be slain by the enemies of the king;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: the king’s servants

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Great Spirit is discussed, not described as appearing.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Ammon or the Great Spirit as present.
Do not stage the earlier encounter involving the flocks as part of this testimony.

title: Lamoni fears he has done wrong
summary: After hearing their words, the king says he believes the Great Spirit has come to preserve their lives. Lamoni fears he may have done wrong in slaying servants; he had slain many after their flocks were scattered at the place of water.
characters: Unnamed people addressed by the king

explicit_facts.text: The king says the Great Spirit has come to preserve the lives of those he addresses.
Lamoni received from his father the tradition that there was a Great Spirit.
Lamoni fears he may have done wrong in slaying his servants.
Lamoni had slain many servants because their flocks had been scattered at the place of water.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lamoni may appear troubled while speaking.
unspecified_visual_details: Lamoni's appearance and posture

spoken_dialogue.text: Now I know that it is the Great Spirit; and he has come down at this time to preserve your lives, that I might not slay you as I did your brethren. Now this is the Great Spirit of whom our fathers have spoken.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The king

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The king's identification of someone as the Great Spirit is his stated belief, not a narrated visible appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the earlier killings or scattering of flocks as happening now.
Do not depict a visible Great Spirit.

title: The practice at Sebus
summary: The verse describes a Lamanite practice at the waters of Sebus: scattering the people's flocks and driving many of the scattered animals to their own land. It identifies this as a practice of plunder.

explicit_facts.text: These Lamanites practiced standing by the waters of Sebus to scatter the flocks of the people.
They did so to drive many of the scattered flocks to their own land; the verse calls it a practice of plunder among them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A waterside landscape with flocks could illustrate the setting of the reported practice without depicting a particular incident.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the Lamanites, flocks, and waters
The number of people or animals visible

narration.text: Now it was the practice of these Lamanites to stand by the waters of Sebus to scatter the flocks of the people, that thereby they might drive away many that were scattered unto their own land, it being a practice of plunder among them.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a report of a customary practice, not an account of a particular attack happening now.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific raid or victim.
Do not portray the Lamanites as driving people, rather than scattered animals, to their own land.

title: Lamoni asks about Ammon
summary: Lamoni asks his servants where Ammon is. They say he is feeding the king's horses. Hearing that Ammon is preparing his horses and chariots, Lamoni is astonished by his faithfulness. Lamoni says he believes Ammon is the Great Spirit and wants him to come in, but dares not.

explicit_facts.text: Lamoni asked his servants where the man with great power was.
The servants said he was feeding Lamoni's horses.
Lamoni had previously commanded his servants to prepare his horses and chariots for travel to the land of Nephi, where Lamoni's father had appointed a feast.
Lamoni heard that Ammon was preparing his horses and chariots and was astonished by Ammon's faithfulness.
Lamoni said he believed Ammon was the Great Spirit and desired him to come in, but dared not.

title: Ammon addresses the king's wonder
summary: Ammon, filled with the Spirit of God, perceives the king's thoughts. He asks whether the king's wonder comes from hearing of Ammon's defense of the servants and flocks. Ammon says he is a man and the king's servant, and will do whatever the king desires that is right.

explicit_facts.text: Ammon, filled with the Spirit of God, perceived the king's thoughts.
Ammon asks whether the king marvels because he has heard that Ammon defended the servants and flocks, slew seven of their brethren with a sling and sword, and smote off others' arms.
Ammon says he is a man and the king's servant, and will do whatever the king desires that is right.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Ammon speaks to the king in person.
unspecified_visual_details: Their appearances, clothing, expressions, and surroundings are not described.

spoken_dialogue.text: Is it because thou hast heard that I defended thy servants and thy flocks, and slew seven of their brethren with the sling and with the sword, and smote off the arms of others, in order to defend thy flocks and thy servants; behold, is it this that causeth thy marvelings?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Ammon

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, I am a man, and am thy servant;

prohibited_inventions: Do not show the earlier fight as occurring during this exchange.

title: Lamoni questions Ammon
summary: King Lamoni marvels that Ammon can discern his thoughts and asks whether Ammon is the Great Spirit. Ammon says he is not. Lamoni asks how Ammon knows his thoughts and by what power he struck those who scattered his flocks. He offers Ammon whatever he desires and says he would guard him with his armies if needed.

explicit_facts.text: The king marveled because he saw that Ammon could discern his thoughts.
Lamoni asked whether Ammon was the Great Spirit, and Ammon answered that he was not.
Lamoni asked how Ammon knew his thoughts and by what power he had struck those who scattered his flocks.
Lamoni offered Ammon whatever he desired and said he would guard him with his armies if needed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lamoni and Ammon are near enough to speak to each other.
unspecified_visual_details: The location and surroundings are not described.
Neither man's appearance or clothing is described.
